name: ObjectDB
tagline: Commercial object database for Java that implements JPA and JDO natively, with no ORM layer.
description: ObjectDB is an object database for Java that implements the JPA and JDO standards directly, so entity classes are stored as objects rather than mapped to tables. That removes ORM overhead and makes it fast for deep object graphs. It runs embedded in the application or as a client-server database and supports JPQL and JDOQL queries, indexes and ACID transactions. A free edition allows up to 10 entity classes and one million objects per file, and commercial server and site licences are inexpensive. It is a niche but steadily maintained choice for Java desktop and server apps that want JPA without Hibernate and SQL.

strengths: Native JPA/JDO with no object-relational mapping layer
Fast traversal of deep object graphs
Embedded or client-server from the same library
weaknesses: Closed source with a single small vendor
Java-only; data is hard to reach from other languages or BI tools
Free edition caps entity classes and object counts
useCases: Java desktop applications with complex object models
JPA-based apps that want to avoid Hibernate tuning
